claims.text: Laser shock peening with controlled nanosecond pulses will refine the near-surface microstructure of Inconel 718.
Laser shock peening will generate a deep, uniform compressive residual-stress profile in Inconel 718.
The treatment will significantly enhance surface hardness relative to untreated Inconel 718.
The treatment will significantly enhance fatigue resistance relative to untreated Inconel 718.
The proposed treatment uses nanosecond laser pulses at approximately 3 J/cm² with an ablative coating and a confining medium at room temperature.
The resulting compressive residual-stress profile will extend several hundred microns into the material.
High-energy laser pulses induce rapid, localized plastic deformation in Inconel 718.
Laser-induced localized plastic deformation refines the near-surface grain structure.
Laser-induced localized plastic deformation establishes compressive residual stresses.
The compressive residual stresses inhibit crack initiation and propagation.
Inhibiting crack initiation and propagation enhances fatigue and wear resistance.
The proposed treatment will increase surface hardness by approximately 25% relative to untreated Inconel 718.
The proposed treatment will improve fatigue life relative to untreated Inconel 718.
The enhanced mechanical properties will be maintained under cyclic mechanical and thermal stresses representative of aggressive environments.
Untreated Inconel 718 has lower surface hardness than the proposed laser-shock-peened material.
Untreated Inconel 718 is more susceptible to fatigue-induced microcrack formation than the proposed treated material under aggressive operating conditions.
Deviations from the specified laser parameters may produce nonuniform residual-stress distributions.
Deviations from the specified laser parameters may cause microcracking.
Performance may be reduced under thermal or mechanical extremes beyond those tested.
